To try it in an app created with `exact new`, replace `app.contract` and `app.test.contract` with the examples below. In `app.ts`, keep the generated `export const appId = …` line and replace the rest with the TypeScript below. ```contract // app.contract: the view, its state, and what each action changes. It names no colour, // font or control size: each host draws its own heading, field, button, checkbox and list. shape Todo id: string title: string done: bool shape Change count: number component Todos state draft = "" mutation changed as shape Change refreshes todos resource todos = todos() as shape Todo[] derive left = todos.filter(t => not t.done).length action edit(value: string) draft = value action add if draft.trim() != "" send changed = addTodo(draft.trim()) draft = "" action toggle(id: string, done: bool) send changed = setDone(id, done) action remove(id: string) send changed = removeTodo(id) view list appearance="auto" height="100%" section header text `${left} left` role="heading" testId="count" row input value=draft input=edit submit=add placeholder="What needs doing?" aria-label="New todo" testId="new-todo" flex=1 min-width=0 button press=add buttonStyle="filled" testId="add" text "Add" section for t in todos key=t.id row testId=`todo-${t.id}` input type="checkbox" checked=t.done change=toggle(t.id) aria-label=t.title testId=`toggle-${t.id}` text t.title flex=1 button press=remove(t.id) destructive=true testId=`remove-${t.id}` text "Delete" ``` ```ts // app.ts: keeps the list, and answers what app.contract asks for import type { Answer, Sources } from './app.contract.d.ts'; export const grants = ''; // e.g. 'net.fetch https://api.example.com' type Todo = { id: string; title: string; done: boolean }; let todos: Todo[] = []; let next = 1; const sources: Sources = { todos: () => todos, addTodo: ([title]) => { todos = [...todos, { id: String(next++), title, done: false }]; return { count: todos.length }; }, setDone: ([id, done]) => { todos = todos.map((t) => (t.id === id ? { ...t, done } : t)); return { count: todos.length }; }, removeTodo: ([id]) => { todos = todos.filter((t) => t.id !== id); return { count: todos.length }; }, }; export const answer: Answer = (source, args, store, storage, native) => sources[source](args, store, storage, native); ``` ```contract-test // app.test.contract: runs on any host with `scripts/agent.mjs --test` test "add, finish and delete" expect text "count" == "0 left" type "new-todo" "Buy milk" tap "add" type "new-todo" "Walk the dog" type "new-todo" key "Enter" expect text "count" == "2 left" tap "toggle-1" expect text "count" == "1 left" tap "remove-1" expect tree missing "todo-1" expect tree has "todo-2" ```
WebmacOSiOS Simulator
The view never edits the list itself. An action `send`s a *mutation* to a source, `app.ts` changes its data and answers, and `refreshes todos` asks for the list again. Data lives in one place, and every change to it is a named, typed call an agent can see. This list lives in memory. To keep it across launches, give `app.ts` a grant like `sqlite.open app:/data/todos.db` and use `storage.sqlite`, as [Fieldnotes](apps/fieldnotes) does. ### The pieces | Concept | What it is | |---|---| | `shape` | A closed record type. Fields are `number`, `string`, `bool`, another shape, `option`, or `T[]`. | | `component` | A unit of UI. The first one in a file is the root. Components take `props`, can `inject` what an ancestor `provide`s, and can fill a `slot` with `children`. | | `state` | A value the component owns, its type inferred or declared (`state picked: option = none`). Under a `for`, child state belongs to that keyed row. | | `derive` | A value computed from others, recomputed when they change. | | `resource` | Data from a source: `resource x = source(args) as shape T`. When the arguments change, the source is asked again. | | `mutation` / `send` | A change made through a source: `send x = source(args)`. `refreshes r` asks resource `r` again afterward, `pending(x)` and `failed(x)` show progress, and `failure(x)` says why a resource failed. | | `action` | The only place state changes. What it writes is inferred from its body, and `let` binds a local inside it. | | `task` | Work on a schedule: `every(1000, tick)`, `after(ms, a)`, `every(frame, a)`. | | `view` | Indented elements, `if … else`, `for … key=…` (a key is required), `match` over options, and calls to other components. | | `style` / `class=` | A named set of CSS properties. The node's own attributes win, and there is no cascade. | | `fn`, `xs.map` / `xs.filter` / `xs.join` | Pure, single-expression helpers. Recursion is refused. | | Built-in functions | The web's string and array methods by their names, called on the value (`xs.length`, `s.trim()`, `s.includes(t)`, `xs.at(-1)`), and functions (`first(xs)`, `formatDate`, `formatNumber`); all are listed with their types under `stdlib` in [`plan/tables/format.json`](plan/tables/format.json). | | `routes` | A router: a location and a retained stack per tab, moved with `open`, `push`, `replace`, and `back`, and read with `top`. | | `font` | Declares a font family and binds it to files at build time. | | `use … from "./x.contract"` | Imports components, shapes, styles, and `fn`s from another Contract file. | | `testId` | A stable name for the agent, tests, and accessibility tools. | ### What Contract leaves out, and why - **No JavaScript in the view, and no I/O.** Expressions have no effects. Effects happen only in actions, as assignments, `send`, `refresh`, or commands like `focus(…)` and `share(…)`. Data crosses one seam: a source answers, and the runner checks the answer. - **No loops in actions, no `await`.** A list is a view's keyed `for`, a computation is a `derive` or a `fn` (an action may name a value with `let`), and anything slower lives in a source. A list that changes changes where its data lives, through a mutation, as in the example above. That's what lets the plan be baked, diffed, inspected, and executed the same way on four hosts. - **No escape hatch; access hatches.** Nothing steps outside the plan. Where an app needs a platform widget, it uses a *native module*: a hyphenated tag like `exact-map`, backed by Swift, Kotlin or Rust, laid out by the kernel like any other box. Where it needs the platform object Exact itself built (a `UIView`, a navigation controller, a DOM element), it marks the node `hatch="word"` and its native code is handed that object: an *access hatch*, the panel a machine is built with so its insides can be reached. It configures what Exact made and changes Contract state only by acting on authored nodes, as a person would. These limits serve the principles. An agent can't wire up a data race it can't write. A plan with no JavaScript in it starts fast. A view written in CSS's own words lays out the same on every host and looks at home on each. ### The compiler talks back ```sh $ cargo run -q -p contract -- build app.contract app.contract:4:5 [type-assign] `count` is `number`, cannot assign `string` app.contract:7:23 [lower-unknown-attr] `text` has no attribute `size`; `size` is spelled `font-size` here, the web's name (LLP 1017 §8.1) ``` One run reports up to twenty independent errors, not just the first. Other subcommands: `--json` for tools, `symbols` (definitions and references as JSON), `fmt` (source-preserving), `types` (generates `app.contract.d.ts` for TypeScript sources), and `rust` (shapes for a Rust data crate). The full language is specified in [LLP 1006](llp/1006-contract-compiler-v1.spec.md), [LLP 1017.000](llp/1017.000-contract-v1-1.spec.md) (v1.1), and [LLP 1017.003](llp/1017.003-map-filter-join.spec.md). Data sources are covered in [LLP 1027](llp/1027-typescript-data-sources.rfc.md). ## Example apps Each app lives in [`apps//`](apps). Run one on the web with `bun host/web/dev.mjs --app `, on macOS with `bun host/apple/build.mjs -apple --run`, and on iOS by adding `--ios`. All of these screenshots come from the web host, taken by `scripts/agent.mjs`. To learn from, start with [Shelf](apps/shelf), the recipe app. It names no colour and no font size, and `scripts/no-tells.mjs` holds it to that, so it shows what an app that leaves presentation to the platform looks like on each host. Then read these four for what each teaches. They were written before [LLP 1115](llp/1115-write-the-web-ship-the-platform.principle.md) and paint their own colours and sizes, so take their structure, not their style: | App | What it teaches | |---|---| | [Caltrain](apps/caltrain) | A Rust data crate, authored tests, routes, an optional GPU module | | [Weatherlight](apps/weatherlight) | TypeScript with `fetch` and grants | | [Fieldnotes](apps/fieldnotes) | Storage: SQLite, files, backup and restore | | [Recorder](apps/recorder) | The microphone through `@exact/media-capture` and `@exact/recording` |
Caltrain
The app that defines v1: nearby stations, live departure boards, search, theming, a Canvas 2D line map, and an aurora GPU sky. Rust data. Every host.		 Weatherlight
Weather from Open-Meteo under a GPU-animated sky that follows the hour you pick. TypeScript data and a wgpu module.		 Spark
A swipe deck: throw a card with your finger, and it flies off with your release velocity. Pan gestures and springs on every host.		 Expose
A pretend phone OS (lock screen, home, Messages with an AI assistant, Reader) set in custom fonts. TypeScript. The assistant needs an OpenRouter key.
Calendar
Month pages, draggable sheets, events dragged between days, wallpaper themes, SQLite. It lives outside apps/, so set EXACT_APP_DIR to run it.		 Sparkline
A market list of animated SVG charts that draw in and pulse.		 Photo Editor
Rotate, pan, and crop, through a native module.		 Video Player
A bundled clip that shrinks out of the way when the keyboard opens.
Exact Live
A creative-production workspace: a photo grid you reorder by dragging, a crew chat that can take a 10,000-message burst, and a Markdown runbook. Rust data.		 Still (Interaction Gallery)
Drag to reorder, pan and zoom photos, a resizable sheet with a nested list, and 100 to 25,000 records.
Reflow
Seven typography studies after Cheng Lou's Pretext demos: text flowing around moving balls, a dragon, masonry, and a magazine spread. Line heights come from font metrics read at build time.		 Textflow
Text around shapes with CSS's shape-outside and wrap-flow: draggable orbs, a dancer, an editorial layout. One Rust walker shared by every host.
Markdown
A Markdown reader that opens files from Finder or the command line (mdview README.md). Its sibling LLP (llpview) reads this repository's design corpus.		 Conduit (RealWorld)
The RealWorld Medium clone against its hosted API. It's the benchmark that compared Exact's web build with React 19. Web only.
SVG Gallery: SVG as the browser renders it, one page per feature, held to Chrome's pixels on every host.
Canvas Gallery: the HTML Canvas 2D API drawn by the browser, Core Graphics, or tiny-skia, and compared to Chrome.
### More apps, labs, and stress tests | App | What it shows | Notes | |---|---|---| | [Fieldnotes](apps/fieldnotes) | A local notebook with pins, search, SQLite storage, and JSON backup and restore | TypeScript + Rust | | [Messages](apps/messages) | A port of Expo's chat demo, talking to models through OpenRouter | Needs `bun apps/messages/service.ts` and an OpenRouter key | | [Type Tour](apps/typetour) | Phone-OS screens as a type specimen for the Expose fonts | No JavaScript at all | | [Map Demo](apps/map-demo) | Native modules: MapKit on Apple and OpenStreetMap on the web | | | [Carousel](apps/carousel) | A horizontal virtualized list of 25,000 cards | | | [Motion Gallery](apps/motion-gallery) | Animated GIF and WebP images and CSS keyframes, compared across hosts | | | [Update Lab](apps/update-lab) | Live replacement of Contract, TypeScript, and Rust in a running app | Hand-testing lab | | [Messages Stress](apps/messages-stress), [Completion Storm](apps/completion-storm), [Markdown Stress](apps/markdown-stress) | 100k-message histories, 128 parallel requests, and 4 MiB documents, under load | Opt-in workloads ([LLP 1041](llp/1041-graceful-overload.rfc.md)) | | [Native Fixture](apps/native-fixture), [Auth Fixture](apps/auth-fixture) | The native-module interface; OAuth with PAR, DPoP, and PKCE against a local server | Test fixtures | | [Beacons, Tennis, …](game/games) | Games on the optional [engine add-on](game/README.md): Rust gameplay, Contract menus | `bun game/dev.mjs beacons` | ## What works today, and what doesn't yet The v1 bar, from `rules/DEFERRED.md`: *one real application, not a demo, runs from a single Contract source on web, macOS, iOS, and Linux, within the time budgets in `rules/RULES.md`.* Caltrain is that application, and it runs on all four. Everything else here was admitted because a real app needed it. ### Working - **Four hosts.** Web, macOS (AppKit, no SwiftUI), iOS (UIKit, on the Simulator and on devices), and Linux (GPU or CPU painting, DRM/KMS or headless). Existing Swift apps can embed Exact sessions through ExactKit ([LLP 1031](llp/1031-brownfield-embedding.rfc.md)). - **Layout and text.** CSS block, flex, and grid; `position: static` and containing blocks; `aspect-ratio`; declared fonts; text around shapes ([LLP 1043.000](llp/1043.000-text-around-shapes.rfc.md)). - **Paint.** Gradients, shadows, `backdrop-filter`, glass materials, complete SVG ([LLP 1055](llp/1055-svg-shapes-and-css-animations.rfc.md)), Canvas 2D on every host ([LLP 1056](llp/1056-canvas-2d.rfc.md)), and a wgpu GPU canvas loaded after first pixel. - **Motion.** CSS transitions, springs, `@keyframes`, follow-and-release gestures (pan, swipe, pinch) with release velocity, layout transitions, exit animations, and scroll- or drag-linked timelines ([LLP 1002](llp/1002-motion-v1.rfc.md), [LLP 1063](llp/1063-presence-and-layout-motion.rfc.md)). - **Lists.** Virtualized lists, vertical or horizontal, one level deep ([LLP 1070](llp/1070-nested-and-horizontal-lists.rfc.md)). The rows of a vertical `list` are its platform's: UIKit's separators and highlight, a table on the Mac, one line between rows on the web, with nothing drawn by the app ([LLP 1115.000](llp/1115.000-no-tells-on-every-host.rfc.md), D16). - **Controls and media.** Inputs, `select`, a WYSIWYG Markdown editor on the web, macOS, and iOS ([LLP 1045](llp/1045-markdown-editor.rfc.md)), images including animated ones, video ([LLP 1042](llp/1042-video.spec.md)), pickers for an app's declared file types, and share. - **Data.** TypeScript or Rust sources, optionally on a worker. Grant-checked `fetch` and streams, files and SQLite (native and in the browser), Keychain secrets, and OAuth sign-in. A router keeps a stack per tab ([LLP 1038](llp/1038-router.rfc.md)). - **Native modules.** Platform widgets as hyphenated tags ([LLP 1024](llp/1024-native-modules.rfc.md)). - **The web, server side.** Pages pre-rendered at build time or per request by a Rust renderer, then adopted in place instead of hydrated ([LLP 1048](llp/1048-rendering-across-the-curve.rfc.md)). - **Delivery.** `scripts/deploy.mjs` publishes the web root and signed update bundles, which installed apps fetch after first pixel. Apple apps check every fifteen minutes while active under every activation policy; `deploy.check.interval` overrides the interval in seconds. Checks stage a candidate; `deploy.activate` controls when it applies. TypeScript and Rust logic can be replaced live in development. Every web build gets an install page, and `exact release` signs and notarizes a Mac app ([LLP 1030](llp/1030-delivery-unified.rfc.md)). - **Agents and tests.** The ten operations on every host, including a physical iPhone; Contract tests; source maps; filmed screenshots. ### Not yet, or not at all - **Windows.** Apps default to ink on a DirectX 11 composition swap chain, or CPU when the manifest declares `game`. `host.windows.painter: "ink"` or `"cpu"` selects either painter, and `EXACT_PAINTER` overrides both. Skirmish is a standalone game built with Exact's optional game engine; the CPU default preserves its module-owned window presentation. See [LLP 1149 D12](llp/1149-the-renderer.rfc.md#d12--where-it-is-the-presenter-and-what-the-same-everywhere-promises). [Windows Desk](apps/windows-desk/README.md) demonstrates native controls over Contract and the kernel with an app-local Win32 presenter; general Windows control parity and delivery remain unfinished. - **Android.** Admitted (2026-10-07) and early. An app builds for Android and runs on an emulator or a phone: `bun exact.mjs android` builds it, `bun exact.mjs test android` runs its tests, and `bun exact.mjs agent android …` drives it ([LLP 1107](llp/1107-driving-an-app-on-android.rfc.md)). It needs the Android SDK, the Rust target `aarch64-linux-android`, and the Hermes Android bundle, which `exact setup` installs with the target. Delivery and store packaging don't exist yet. - **No JSX or React tier.** Nothing runs JavaScript above the data seam. The door stays open, but no one is building it. - **TypeScript can't import npm packages' code yet.** `app.ts` imports its own local files; from a package it imports only types (`import type`), which the build checks and never runs. - **Code updates in production.** Signed delivery covers plans and assets. Signed delivery of TypeScript or Rust modules isn't implemented, and app-store rules limit it anyway. - **Linux editing.** The web and Apple hosts edit; Linux reads. Linux also has no word segmenter, so flowed Thai, Lao, Khmer, and Myanmar text breaks only at spaces. - **Out on purpose for v1.** Camera access, a gesture arena, general layout animation, grid or masonry virtualization, a general webview beyond `iframe`, and a devtools UI. - **No packaged CLI.** You work from a source checkout. `exact new` apps refer to it by path. [`QUEUE.md`](QUEUE.md) lists what would make sense to do next, and [`llp/current/`](llp/current) holds the design documents in play. ## Repository map | Path | What's there | |---|---| | [`kernel/`](kernel) | `exact-kernel`: the node arena, wire frames, transactions, Taffy layout, and the export. [`kernel/tables/schema.json`](kernel/tables/schema.json) declares every node type, property, and opcode. | | [`contract/`](contract) | The Contract compiler (`syntax` → `types` → `analyze` → `lower`), its CLI, and the corpus | | [`plan/`](plan), [`runner/`](runner) | The plan format, generated from one JSON authority, and the VM that runs it | | [`motion/`](motion) | CSS transitions, springs, and the seekable clock for non-web hosts | | [`host/`](host) | `web/`, `web-js/` (the JS target), `apple/` (Rust core, ExactKit Swift package, AppKit and UIKit), `linux/`, `render/` (server pages), plus update adapters and rasterizers | | [`js/`](js), [`logic/`](logic), [`data/`](data) | The TypeScript executor (Hermes, and the browser's engine on the web), Rust logic modules, and the data seam | | [`gpu/`](gpu), [`canvas/`](canvas), [`textflow/`](textflow), [`markdown/`](markdown) | Capabilities loaded on demand: the wgpu canvas, Canvas 2D, text around shapes, and the Markdown editor | | [`route/`](route), [`update/`](update), [`bake/`](bake), [`filesystem/`](filesystem) | The router, the signed update store, delivery baking, and app-owned files | | [`apps/`](apps), [`examples/`](examples), [`game/`](game) | The apps above, the Calendar example, and the optional game engine | | [`scripts/`](scripts) | `exact.mjs`, `agent.mjs`, `smoke.mjs`, `metrics.mjs`, `deploy.mjs`, and the checks | | [`llp/`](llp) | The design corpus: numbered RFCs, specs, and research ([LLP 1000](llp/1000-exact2-root.explainer.md) is the map) | | [`rules/`](rules) | [`RULES.md`](rules/RULES.md) and [`DEFERRED.md`](rules/DEFERRED.md), the two binding documents | | [`vendor/taffy/`](vendor/taffy) | Taffy, plus Exact's patches | ## Working on Exact Start with [`rules/RULES.md`](rules/RULES.md), one page on how work happens here, and [`rules/DEFERRED.md`](rules/DEFERRED.md), what v1 deliberately leaves out. Agents should also read [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). In short: - **Six blocking checks, 65 seconds in total.** Anything slower runs asynchronously, per commit. ```sh cargo build --all-targets --keep-going cargo test --tests --no-fail-fast cargo clippy --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all -- --check bun scripts/caps.mjs # budgets: 1,500 lines per source file, document caps bun scripts/boot.mjs # counts the module graph before first pixel cargo check --workspace --all-targets --keep-going # every crate compiles ``` The first three build and test Cargo's `default-members`. The last compiles every other crate too, so a host or an app outside them cannot stop compiling unseen. It needs the pinned Bun (`package.json`) first on `PATH`: app crates' build scripts run it. - **Verify by running, not by reading.** Build the app a change touches and drive it: `bun scripts/smoke.mjs ` drives the whole app on that host. - **Delete; don't deprecate.** Before 1.0 there are no compatibility shims. Generated files are built, never committed. - **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none** (checks, scripts, registries, design documents) without a person saying so. - **Design happens in LLPs.** These are numbered documents in [`llp/`](llp). A spec gets written only when it has an implementer and a date. Detailed operational notes cover toolchains, the Contract CLI's JSON formats, source maps, TypeScript and Rust data modules, storage, live replacement, delivery trust, the install page, and the stress harnesses. They're in [`docs/reference.md`](docs/reference.md). Open issues are files under [`issues/`](issues) ([how that works](docs/issues.md)). The workspace is MIT-licensed (`Cargo.toml`). Exact’s Snapback4 adapter uses published **0.4.33** with the matching immutable Rust source revision `3653cae823145170df3e720f5e321bd1b5b4d79d`. See [the adapter guide](snapback4/README.md) for wiring and device rebuilds.

items.readme_text:
raea

Render Anything Engine (for Anyone)

Tell your AI what to make. Videos, motion graphics, 3D and games, written as React and TypeScript
(the code your AI already writes) and rendered on your own GPU, faster than they play.

raea.io · Made in raea · Why raea · Docs · Releases

--- > **Canary.** raea changes daily. Releases run on macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux (x86_64) and, new and least tested, > Windows (x86_64). Expect breaking changes, rough edges and gaps in the docs. ## Install ```sh curl -fsSL https://raea.io/install | sh ``` The installer puts the `raea` command under `~/.raea`, links it into `~/.local/bin`, and adds raea's agent skills to `~/.claude/skills`, so Claude Code (or any agent that reads that folder) knows how to write, render and check raea work. Run it again to update. The engine is free and needs no account. Tarballs and checksums are on the [releases page](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea/releases). On Windows 10 or 11, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://raea.io/install.ps1 | iex ``` It does the same under `~\.raea` and adds raea to your PATH. raea needs the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64), which most machines already have, and a DirectX 12 or Vulkan GPU driver. ## Hello A composition is a React component that draws a frame for a given moment: ```tsx import { AbsoluteFill, Composition, interpolate, registerRoot, useCurrentFrame } from "raea"; function Hello() { const f = useCurrentFrame(); return Hello; } registerRoot(() => ); ``` ```sh raea render hello.tsx -o hello.mp4 ``` On an Apple Silicon Mac those 90 frames render in about a second. The same file can play live as a game (`raea play`), render one frame for an agent to look at (`-o frame.png --frame 45`), or be checked against a quality floor (`raea check hello.mp4`). `raea init` starts a project, and `raea --help` lists every verb. ## What it does - **Video and motion graphics.** Layout, text, Tailwind, SVG and animation, composited on the GPU and encoded in hardware where the machine has it. Footage is cut by what's said in it (`raea cut`), and `raea check` catches clipped text, low contrast, unsafe areas, freezes and loudness problems before anyone watches. - **Games.** Input, physics, sound and 3D, played live with `raea play`, and exported as a program of their own (`raea export-game`). - **3D.** Scenes in TypeScript drawn by [Bevy](https://bevyengine.org) 0.20: cameras, lights, materials, glTF models, Gaussian splats, and Bevy plugins compiled into the engine. - **Sound.** One mixer for live play and offline render, instruments and effects, and local models for foley and instrument notes (`raea sao`, `raea tokensynth`). - **Built for agents.** Everything it draws stays queryable as data, so an agent can render a frame, look at it, and fix what's wrong without a person in the loop. ## Use it from your agent - **Agent skills.** They live in [raea-skills](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea-skills), pinned here as [`skills/`](skills): `raea` teaches an agent to write, render and check raea compositions, 3D and games included. The installer adds it to `~/.claude/skills`, and `raea skills install --agent NAME` to other agents. - **Claude Code plugin.** `/plugin marketplace add shinyobjectz/raea`, then `/plugin install raea@raea`. - **Craft guides.** `raea guide` prints the floor every edit is held to and the guides for pitches, explainers, stories, games, motion, music and layout. `raea context PROJECT` says what to read before working on a project. ## Build from source Requirements: [Rust](https://rustup.rs) (rustup reads the pinned version from rust-toolchain.toml), [bun](https://bun.sh) and CMake. On macOS, Xcode's command-line tools; on Linux, the ALSA, fontconfig, udev, xkbcommon (with its X11 part, which the app targets' windows also load at run time) and Vulkan libraries and NASM (Ubuntu: `cmake ninja-build nasm libasound2-dev libfontconfig1-dev libudev-dev libvulkan-dev libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-dev`), as public CI installs them. ```sh git clone https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea && cd raea cargo build --release -p raea-cli --no-default-features for d in sdk/raea sdk/react/js sdk/react/tw; do (cd $d && bun install); done target/release/raea render sdk/react/bench/games/pong/edit.tsx -o pong.mp4 ``` `--no-default-features` builds the public engine, as the releases are. The default features add one hosted service, Content Credentials signed by raea's signing server, which isn't part of this repository. raea sends nothing on its own: no telemetry, crash reports or update checks. What reaches the network is what you ask for (a remote URL in a composition, a model downloaded on first use, a `raea gen` step on a provider you hold a key for), and `RAEA_OFFLINE=1` refuses all of it. [docs/settings.md](docs/settings.md) lists the settings raea reads. ## What's in here The workspace is layered, from pure building blocks up to the command. | Folder | What | |---|---| | [`core/`](core) | Pure building blocks: the kernel language (K, interpreted on the CPU and compiled to WGSL), easing and animation, shapes, fonts, the scene and wire formats | | [`gpu/`](gpu) | The one shared GPU device and its telemetry | | [`io/`](io) | Decode and encode (VideoToolbox, software codecs, AV1, a muxer), files, network, npm packages, traces | | [`systems/`](systems) | Engine systems: layout, canvas, compositing, filters, mixing, speech, ML on ONNX Runtime, footage reading, lighting, contact checks for 3D parts, splats | | [`runtime/`](runtime) | Running a composition: the JavaScript engine seam (JavaScriptCore on macOS, QuickJS elsewhere), React and HTML on Bevy, baking, encode, live play | | [`engine/`](engine) | The renderer (`engine/render`), the in-process TypeScript bundler, the Bevy plugin catalog, and the `raea` command itself (`engine/cli`) | | [`apps/`](apps) | The crates behind the CLI's verbs: check, play, games, media | | [`sdk/`](sdk) | `raea`, the TypeScript SDK (`sdk/raea`), its 3D, physics, audio, video and UI packages, the craft guides, and the agent skills | | [`vendor/`](vendor) | Patched upstream crates, under their own licences ([`vendor/vendor.toml`](vendor/vendor.toml) says why each is patched) | | [`tools/`](tools) | Build and release helpers | Behaviour specs written in Gherkin (`.feature`) sit beside the code they describe. ## Licence raea is under the [Functional Source License 1.1, ALv2 Future License](LICENSE) (FSL-1.1-ALv2), copyright Shane Murphy.
